correctness.rationale: Fourier orthogonality reduces the complete infinite-parameter claim to weighted signed-digit equality. For r<b the zero carry is forced at every digit. At r=b the integer carry states remain in {-1,0,1}, with exact binomial matrix entries. Its symmetric two-dimensional sector gives the quadratic recurrence; discriminant and binomial inequalities establish both positive spectral weights and sharp leading root. Direct integer convolution independently matched 281 finite tests. No finite test replaces the all-base proof.

evidence: Diaconis–Fulman (2008) gives a Markov carries matrix for unrestricted uniform digits and unconditioned output digits; its eigenvalues are powers of the reciprocal base.

The present critical transfer has eigenvalues given by the two roots of a quadratic depending on central binomial coefficients, and uses a pinned-zero weighted difference of two binomial digit sums.
